text:
tamir: quick FYI - hit a weird bug today where the python client crashes while parsing rate/quota headers from a partner proxy. debug log attached.

tamir: raw headers we saw:```
RateLimit-Limit: "60;w=60"
RateLimit-Remaining: "0"
Retry-After: 6
X-Client-Quota: {"pool":"alpha","limit":200,"used":200}
RateLimit-Limit: 100
RateLimit-Remaining: 50
```

ash: ack. two issues: 1) mixed formats (string meta + ints) and duplicate RateLimit sets (per-route + global). 2) our async guard pattern does per-task sleep on Retry-After which leads to thundering-herd when many coros wake.

li-wei: for the duplicate RL sets we should collapse to the most restrictive: pick the lowest remaining and earliest reset window. also need to tolerate "60;w=60" and "0" as strings.

ravi: on the throttler: current code is basically:```python
# simplified
async def call():
    if headers.remaining == 0:
        await asyncio.sleep(headers.retry_after)
    return await do_request()
```
That obviously lets N coros sleep then compete after sleep.

ash: suggested design: central AsyncRateLimiter that maintains a token count and a single refill task. API:```python
class AsyncRateLimiter:
    def __init__(...): ...
    async def acquire(self, n=1): ...  # waits until tokens available
    async def __aenter__(self): await self.acquire(); return self
    async def __aexit__(self, *a): self.release()
```
and usage `async with client.rate_limiter.guard():` so only one place manages timing.

tamir: agree. plus header normalizer that returns a small dataclass/TypedDict with canonical types: limit:int|None, remaining:int|None, reset_unix:float|None, retry_after:float|None, quota_pool:str|None. keep callers free of string parsing.

li-wei: sketch for normalize (handles multiple RateLimit headers):```python
def normalize_rate_headers(hdrs: Mapping[str,str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    # collect all RateLimit-* groups, parse ints robustly, parse X-Client-Quota json if present,
    # collapse by choosing lowest remaining and earliest reset, return typed fields
```
we should log a single warning event if parsing falls back, with the raw header snapshot.

ravi: concurrency detail: token bucket refill math must use monotonic time and atomic claims. e.g. maintain last_refill = monotonic(), accumulate tokens = min(capacity, tokens + rate*(now-last_refill)). use an asyncio.Lock around acquire/release and have `acquire` wait on a condition variable rather than sleeping per-task.

ash: +1 on Condition approach: that avoids per-task sleeping and can wake only enough waiters. also add jitter to any backoff we expose to callers to avoid synchronized retry waves.

tamir: tests: param test for header formats ("60", "60;w=60", numbers, missing), multi-header collapse, X-Client-Quota precedence, stress test: spawn 32 coros, mock server that returns Remaining=0+Retry-After, assert post-retry total requests <= capacity+burst.

li-wei: typing: provide py.typed and explicit stub for AsyncRateLimiter to satisfy mypy. normalize_rate_headers should have a narrow return type so downstream code doesn't need repeated casts.

ravi: minor: some infra puts Retry-After in milliseconds or as a non-int. normalizer should parse floats and clamp small negatives to zero.

tamir: I'll open a short RFC PR with the API surface and tests. (will include examples and a small internal benchmark for overshoot).

ci-bot: created issue #3521: "py-sdk: robust header normalizer + central async rate limiter to avoid thundering-herd" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3521)

ash: we'll also add a small note in the onboarding README: "SDK will prefer X-Client-Quota for quota routing; RateLimit-* used for best-effort rate info".

tamir: action items: tamir draft RFC/PR, li-wei adds typed normalize and mypy changes, ravi implements AsyncRateLimiter with Lock+Condition and stress tests, ash documents edge cases. target: ship in patch release next week.

li-wei: I'll add a unit that simulates multiple RateLimit header groups and ensure collapse picks the strictest.

ravi: will prototype Condition-based waiter and share perf numbers.

tamir: thanks all, will ping PR when ready :rocket:
